newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom calls and puts busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom calls and puts busy.

text.p: Options on shares of WorldCom Inc were active again Thursday as the shares fell in heavy trading.
Traders said takeover speculation had not abated while put sellers emerged in force.
"It's very crazy," a trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange said. "They're still buying and selling a lot of calls today but a lot of puts are trading.
"This is the first time we've had big put sellers," he said, explaining that a large customer was selling the January 20 and 22-1/2 puts in particular.
The January 20 put traded about 2,950 contracts by 1130 CST/1730 GMT and the January 22-1/2 put traded 560. Other active WorldCom puts included the December 22-1/2, which traded about 1,350.
Call interest was focused on the January 25s, which traded roughly 4,160. The option had open interest of 15,179 and included an addition of more than 1,700 contracts Wednesday.
WorldCom shares were down 1-1/4 at 21-7/8 on volume of more than 8.3 million shares.
Increased call activity in the last few sessions had traders thinking that takeover speculation was on the rise. Along with the increased volume, volatilities surged as well.
WorldCom has often been named as a potential takeover target by traders and analysts, particularly with the continued consolidation in the telecommunications industry.
Traders noted that despite the takeover speculation and the heavy call buying, WorldCom shares look weak from a technical perspective.
WorldCom's acquisition of MFS Communications Co Inc is expected to close by the end of the year, and some traders said the heightened options activity could relate to that.
Little trading was seen Wednesday in MFS options, but on Thursday, with the stock losing 2-7/8 to 45-5/8, a couple of options saw strong order flow.
The MFS January 50 call traded 1,970 contracts on the Pacific Stock Exchange and 2,370 contracts on the Chicago Board Options Exchange. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com))
